evidence: orchestrator 2026-09-28: plan-2026-09-27.json (2026-09-27-b1efed done, no commit) and plan-2026-09-27-2.json (2026-09-27-06cd9b done at 2e83fb11f; 2026-09-27-c989c6 deviated, shipped_commit 'see git log: triage 2026-09-27 c989c6 (this commit)') passed -Closing with commits on origin/main; the three ids were still open this morning and triage-due printed them as DUE RETURNs

items.root_cause: closing a queue id is the orchestrator's LAST step (triage-close.ps1 after triage-land.ps1), and a run that ends before it leaves the plan finished and the queue open; triage-due read only the queue and the RETURN rule, so a finished, landed item looked exactly like fresh work and was routed for a second diagnosis. 5 occurrences in 2 days (the three 09-27 ids, 735ea6, a30920).

root_fix.what: triage-due names such an id CLOSE-ONLY and gives it no RETURN line
root_fix.exact_change: triage-return-lib.ps1: Get-TriageCloseOnly (open id whose NEWEST plan item is done|deviated|superseded, count 1, shipped_commit null or landed through an injected predicate) and Format-TriageCloseOnlyLine; triage-due.ps1 prints the CLOSE-ONLY lines after the DUE list and skips those ids in the RETURN block; its landed predicate is git merge-base --is-ancestor for a hash and 'the plan file is on origin/main' for the '(this commit)' text. Fails toward DUE: unlanded, unknown, re-fired (count > 1) or no predicate stays DUE.

items.leaves_open: nothing: the CLOSE-ONLY line puts the close in front of the orchestrator on the next tick, and closing stays the orchestrator's by design (agents never close)
